q: Which is the highest mountain in the Alps?
note: At about 4,808 metres it sits on the French-Italian border, well clear of the Matterhorn.

q: Which is the highest mountain in Japan?
note: The 3,776-metre cone last erupted in 1707 and is still classed as an active volcano.

q: Which river flows past St. Louis and Memphis on its way to the Gulf of Mexico?
note: Its delta below New Orleans pushes new land out into the Gulf every year.

q: What is the capital of Argentina?
note: The name means 'good airs', and its residents are known as portenos, 'people of the port'.

q: Which sea lies north of Turkey, also bordered by Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia?
note: Its only natural outlet to the wider ocean is the narrow Bosphorus at Istanbul.

q: Reykjavik is the capital of which island country?
note: It is the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state, just south of the Arctic Circle.

q: Which strait separates Alaska from Russia?
note: Only about 82 kilometres wide, it is the boundary between Asia and North America.

q: The Great Salt Lake lies in which US state?
note: It has no outlet to the sea, so evaporation leaves the water several times saltier than the ocean.

q: Which is larger in land area: Australia or Greenland?
note: Australia is more than three times the size; the Mercator map projection hugely inflates anything near the poles.

q: Which lies further west: Reno, Nevada or Los Angeles, California?
note: California's coast bends sharply east below Point Conception, leaving Los Angeles east of most of Nevada's western edge.

q: Which African country contains more ancient pyramids than Egypt?
note: The Nubian kingdom of Kush built around 200 steep-sided pyramids, roughly double Egypt's tally.

q: Greenland is an autonomous territory within which European kingdom?
note: That makes a small Scandinavian country the sovereign power over the world's largest island.

q: The Dutch parliament, government and royal palace all sit in The Hague, but which city is the official capital of the Netherlands?
note: The Dutch constitution names Amsterdam as capital while leaving the seat of government in The Hague.

q: The canary bird is named after the Canary Islands, but the islands themselves are named after which animal?
note: Roman writers called the group Insulae Canariae, 'islands of the dogs', from the Latin canis.

q: Which of the five Great Lakes lies entirely within the United States?
note: The Canadian border runs through the other four; Michigan is the only one wholly in US waters.

q: Which sea separates Australia from New Zealand?
note: Named for Abel Tasman, who crossed it in 1642; the crossing is known locally as 'the ditch'.

q: Which opened to shipping first: the Suez Canal or the Panama Canal?
note: Suez opened in 1869, forty-five years before Panama's locks finally opened in 1914.

q: Which was begun first: the Great Wall of China or the Colosseum in Rome?
note: Chinese states were building defensive walls centuries BC; the Colosseum was finished in AD 80.

q: Which park, established in 1872, is generally regarded as the world's first national park?
note: Congress set it aside before Wyoming, Montana or Idaho were even states.

q: Which continent is divided into more countries than any other?
note: Africa holds 54 sovereign states, comfortably ahead of Asia's 49.

q: Which Caribbean island is shared between Haiti and the Dominican Republic?
note: It is the only Caribbean island split between two sovereign countries.

q: Which is the highest mountain in South America?
note: At about 6,961 metres in Argentina, it is the highest peak anywhere outside Asia.

q: Victoria Falls sits on the border between which two African countries?
note: The Zambezi drops into a chasm the locals call Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'.

q: Easter Island, famous for its giant stone heads, is a territory of which country?
note: Chile annexed it in 1888; the island lies some 3,500 kilometres west of the mainland.

q: Which lies further east: Miami, Florida or Santiago, Chile?
note: South America sits far to the east of where most people picture it; Santiago is about ten degrees of longitude east of Miami.

q: The northernmost point of mainland Africa lies in which country?
note: Cap Angela, near Bizerte, beats anything in Morocco or Egypt by a comfortable margin.

q: Measured from its base on the ocean floor rather than from sea level, which Hawaiian mountain is the tallest on Earth?
note: Base to summit it rises over 10,000 metres, though only 4,207 of those are above the waves.

q: Which Ecuadorian volcano's summit is the point on land furthest from the centre of the Earth?
note: The planet bulges at the equator, so a 6,263-metre equatorial peak outreaches Everest from the core.

q: Only two countries in the world are doubly landlocked, surrounded entirely by other landlocked countries. Name them.
note: Liechtenstein is ringed by Switzerland and Austria; Uzbekistan's neighbours are all landlocked too, as the Caspian is a lake.

q: Which was completed first: the Hoover Dam or the Golden Gate Bridge?
note: The dam was dedicated in 1935, nearly two years before the bridge opened in May 1937.
